hypothesis: A prompt chunk of the qwen36 CUDA chain stages a layer's experts from the tier's host pool in one buffer, and the copy of the next staged layer waits until this layer's experts were read, so a layer's MoE and the next copy run in line. With the residents spread over the layers (a Colab T4 holding 6605 of the 10240 experts: 91 experts to copy a layer, the copy and the layer's kernels ~15 ms each) two staging places, the staged layers taking them in turn, let the copy run beside the layer before: the 512-token prompt alone gets faster, and the logits are what they were.
command: bench.c built against c/ (cd c && make <objects> CUDA=1 CUDA_ARCH=sm_75, as bench build does); COLI_CUDA=1 COLI_GPUS=0 CUDA_EXPERT_GB=auto OMP_WAIT_POLICY=ACTIVE OMP_PROC_BIND=close ./qwen36-bench --model <model> --text promessi_sposi.txt --lengths 512 --gen 1 --teacher
